why: A track position written out longhand at the consumer instead of taken from the shared model -- the exact shape `makeTank` had before issue #385, and the way an exported tank silently stops being the tank the game draws. The tracks move from the model's +/-0.375 (HULL_WIDTH/2 - TRACK_W/2) to +/-0.3, which pulls them visibly inward off the hull's edge. WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS RATHER THAN A COMPARISON OF THE TWO BUILDERS: `makeTank` calls `tankParts()`, so a test that checked the model against itself would be comparing a function to its own output and could not fail. The risk is at the CONSUMER, and it is measured: with this mutation applied, `src/render/entities.test.ts` passes 90 of 90 -- the whole existing render suite is blind to it, because nothing there asserts where a track sits -- while `tank-model.test.ts` fails 1 of 7, on the case that compares the live scene graph's track offsets against the model's. That gap between 90-of-90 green and one named failure is the coverage this issue added. Scoped to tank-model.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
